WIC6-01.note: Key is right and the coverage sentence does the work. 'empirical' is the strongest distractor on the batch and comes close to surviving, since whole-sky-every-night coverage is itself an evidentiary gain, but the passage concedes the photometer's thousand-fold precision, which is the only evidence claim it makes, so the grounds left standing are about arranging observers.

WIC6-02.free_elimination: REAL: 'not something the marsh survives but something it ___' forbids 'withstands', which is a bare synonym of 'survives'. Pure lexical knowledge, no passage needed, so one of four is free.
WIC6-02.note: Clean item apart from the free strike on 'withstands'. 'invites' and 'measures' both need the silt mechanism to kill, so the passage still earns its place, but the effective field is three.

WIC6-03.read_aloud_flag: 'malformed' is a computing/data register word ('malformed input', 'malformed XML'); the idiomatic English for a question with an unspecified referent is 'ill-posed'. A geodesist saying a question is malformed does not sound like speech.
WIC6-03.note: The explanation's defence of the key is wrong: 'unanswerable' does not require the measurements to be out of reach, only that the question as asked has no single answer, which is precisely what the last sentence asserts. 'Which is better, chocolate or vanilla' is unanswerable with both quantities in hand. Two options survive and the more natural one is not the key.

WIC6-04.read_aloud_flag: 'settlement' carries a geotechnical sense - the downward movement of a ground surface - and the passage says 'the surface sinks', so the on-topic technical reading of the distractor is literally described in the text. It is killable (compacted peat would still be present) but only on the oxidation sentence.
WIC6-04.free_elimination: MISSED, partial: 'drainage' echoes 'drained' in the first clause, and a test-wise student strikes the verbatim-root echo without reading. 'evaporation' is also close to a collocation kill - a post does not measure evaporation.
WIC6-04.note: Best-built item in the batch: the not-X-but-Y frame gives nothing away, and the key is forced by one clause ('oxidizes into the air') that the strongest rival cannot survive. The morphological echo on 'drainage' is the only leak.

WIC6-05.free_elimination: MISSED: 'not the signature of a place but of a ___' is a stock opposition, and 'person' is the only option in the set that is the categorical complement of 'place'. Striking the other three is not the same act as solving the item - it is done on the frame alone.
WIC6-05.note: A vocabulary question wearing a passage, and the weakest item here on the terms of this half. The blank sentence alone decides it via place/person; the sequencing evidence is decorative. 'lineage' is the only distractor that asks anything, and it dies to the same frame.

WIC6-06.note: 'outgrown' is the precise answer and the size clause supports it, but the passage also states flatly that traffic left for estuaries miles downstream, which makes 'the harbor had abandoned them' true on the passage's own facts rather than merely imprecise. The explanation's counter - that 'abandoned' omits the reason and implies desertion - is a preference, not an exclusion.

WIC6-07.free_elimination: DECLARED ELIMINATION IS NOT REAL AS SCOPED: 'decisive' is struck only by noticing that the word before 'until' must be dismissive, and that single inference is the whole item - it kills 'plausible' and 'decisive' together. Making the elimination and solving are the same act, so it is not free.
WIC6-07.note: 'secondary' survives on the passage's own account: the suggestion is introduced third, and the footage plus the range correlation promote it to the leading explanation, so 'looked secondary until someone filmed the flies' is exactly the reversal the sentence describes. The explanation concedes this ('makes it the leading one rather than a lesser contributor') while treating it as a refutation.

WIC6-08.read_aloud_flag: 'a record of medieval durability' is a slightly clunky abstract-noun collocation; 'of what lasted' is how one would actually say it. Not wrong, but it is the least natural of the four completions, which cuts against the key.
WIC6-08.free_elimination: REAL: 'a record of medieval ___ rather than of medieval housing' will not take 'settlement', which is a near-synonym of housing in this register, so the rather-than frame forbids it without any passage. Cheap and genuine.
WIC6-08.note: Genuinely hard and the survivorship reasoning is real; 'carpentry' is a strong rival that needs the whole two-wall-types contrast to kill. Holds.

WIC6-09.free_elimination: DECLARED ELIMINATION IS NOT REAL: 'mutation' is struck by reading 'already carrying them' in the blank sentence, which is meaning, not frame. It is a cheap strike, not a free one. MISSED and closer to free: 'compounds' appears verbatim in the passage, and the verbatim echo is a standard steer away from an option.
WIC6-09.note: Key is correct and exclusive - the selection reading is the only one that explains a change in proportions. Demoted from hard: once 'already carrying them' is read, three options fall in one pass and 'advantage' is an ordinary word.

WIC6-10.free_elimination: DECLARED ELIMINATION IS NOT REAL: 'a fiction its readers exposed' is perfectly grammatical and idiomatic; it is ruled out only by knowing that the drivers made the fiction true instead of visible, which is the item. No frame constraint operates here.
WIC6-10.note: The best item in the batch. The key is figurative, arrives from nowhere in the option set, and demands the whole anecdote; 'resented' is the only weak option. Genuinely hard.

WIC6-11.free_elimination: REAL: 'not rare; he was ___' forbids 'unusual' outright as a restatement, on lexical knowledge alone. MISSED: 'unmeasured' echoes 'measured' from the first sentence, a second steer off a distractor, so the frame plus the echo leave two.
WIC6-11.note: Key is right and follows directly from 'the answer was none'. Two of four options are strikable before any reasoning, which keeps this at medium and no higher.

WIC6-12.read_aloud_flag: 'Each one disciplined a performance' is an awkward transitive use: 'discipline' takes a person or appears attributively ('disciplined prose'), and a printed text disciplining a performance is a literary stretch rather than plain English. The oddity steers a careful reader away from the key.
WIC6-12.note: The author's own worry is correct and worse than it thought: the preceding sentence is 'The printed texts are not transcriptions', and transcription/translation is the stock opposition, so 'Each one translated a performance that changed from verse to verse' reads as the sentence the paragraph set up. The blank sentence also carries the changed-versus-fixed contrast on its own, so the notebooks are not strictly needed.
